subject: Startups
title: The Term Sheet Explained
description: A quick win: understand The Term Sheet Explained.

hook.text: A term sheet is a short document that outlines how much a VC will invest and what they'll get in return.

buildup.text: Key terms include valuation, board seats, liquidation preferences, and anti-dilution protections.

discovery.text: Valuation gets all the attention, but liquidation preference matters more—it decides who gets paid first in a sale.

twist.text: A startup with a $100M valuation can still leave founders with nothing if liquidation preferences stack up.

climax.text: Smart founders negotiate term sheets carefully. The headline number matters less than the fine print.

punchline.text: The valuation makes headlines. The terms make money.

quiz.question: Why is liquidation preference important in a term sheet?
options: It decides who gets paid first in a sale
